subject: SDK: client-priority header causing tail-latency spike — field triage & roadmap ask
messages:
From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sam Ortega <sam.ortega@integrishealth.com>
Date: Wed, 10 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: SDK: client-priority header causing tail-latency spike — quick triage ask

Team —

During yesterday's live pilot with Integris Health we observed a recurring tail-latency spike (p95->p99) on text-generation for several patient-summary requests. Attached I dropped an anonymized trace (trace_dump_20260610.json). The customer is seeing intermittent 700–1100ms token latencies while their normal baseline is ~120–180ms.

Observations from the field eng session (Sam on the thread):
- The Integris mobile client attaches a custom header `X-Client-Priority: high` for certain clinical flows.
- When that header is present, their request throughput becomes bursty and we see requests routed into a higher-concurrency worker group which appears to deschedule KV-cache locality, increasing cold-KV reads.
- The impact is worst for longer sequences (>512 tokens) and for requests that hit variant routing (they use a pinned model alias).

Ask: can platform/runtime team do an initial triage to confirm whether header-driven routing or the SDK/edge layer is causing sharding that breaks caching locality? If we can get an interim mitigation (server-side mapping of `X-Client-Priority` -> soft-priority flag that doesn't change pool affinity) that would buy time while we scope a proper SDK change.

Customer impact: Integris is mid-pilot; procurement is paused until we can show stable latency for clinical flows. This is on the critical path for DEAL-4583.

Action items I propose (short):
1) Runtime: validate routing logs for traces that include `X-Client-Priority` (I attached trace) — confirm whether routing policy picks a different capacity tier.
2) SDK/Product: evaluate a short-term SDK opt-in flag (e.g., priority_mode: "soft") that sets metadata without changing pool routing.
3) Sales Eng / Customer: provide a canary rollout plan to Integris (reduce concurrency or disable header while we ship).

I can jump on a quick call if helpful.

—Neha
Neha Kapoor
Principal Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sam Ortega <sam.ortega@integrishealth.com>
Date: Wed, 10 Jun 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SDK: client-priority header causing tail-latency spike — quick triage ask

Thanks Neha — I pulled the trace and a couple of routing logs. Initial findings:

- The `X-Client-Priority` header is being treated by the routing layer as a hard-pref for the "low-latency" pool because of an older routing rule that looks at any client-specified priority header. That pool currently has smaller KV-cache sizes per-instance to maintain tight latency at low qps, which explains the increased cold KV reads for longer sequences.
- The SDK itself isn't modifying pool affinity; it's the upstream edge/router that reads the header and maps to the pool.

Short-term mitigation I can push (server-side):
- Add a translation rule: `X-Client-Priority` -> metadata.priority=soft (no pool affinity change) for Integris' project id. I can gate by project to avoid global behavior change. ETA: ~24 hours for prod rule and smoke tests.

Longer-term ask for Product/SDK:
- Provide an explicit SDK flag (priority_mode: [none|soft|hard]) with clear semantics in the SDK and API docs. Default should be `none`. `soft` should be purely signaling and should not affect routing unless paired with an account-level policy.
- Add telemetry tags to traces to indicate whether a request went through affinity-based routing so we can correlate p99 spikes with routing decisions.

CC'ing Marissa and Soojin for product & rollout implications.

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Staff Engineer, Serving Runtime

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>, Sam Ortega <sam.ortega@integrishealth.com>
Date: Thu, 11 Jun 2026 09:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SDK: client-priority header causing tail-latency spike — quick triage ask

Appreciate the fast triage — this matches a broader product question about how we define "priority" in the public API. A few product notes:

- From a UX/contract standpoint we need two things: (1) a stable, documented SDK flag for customers to express importance without surprising routing changes; (2) account-level policies that operators can opt into for hard-priority routing (e.g., pay-for-priority).
- Proposal: add `priority_mode` to SDKs + API schema and an account flag `enable_hard_priority_routing`. If account flag is off, `priority_mode=hard` should be rejected or downmapped to `soft` with a notice.
- We should avoid allowing arbitrary headers to influence pool selection. Routing rules should prefer authenticated account policies + server-side overrides.

For the Integris pilot: agree with Karthik's server-side gated translation as the fastest patch. I'll schedule a small product review to scope the SDK change (impact across Python/JS/Go) and the API contract versioning.

Action: Marissa will own SDK feature scoping; Karthik will own runtime gating change; Neha will keep customer communications and confirm the canary plan.

Marissa Cole
Director, Product — Redwood Inference

From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sam Ortega <sam.ortega@integrishealth.com>
Date: Fri, 12 Jun 2026 16:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SDK: client-priority header causing tail-latency spike — quick triage ask

Quick update:

- Runtime rule deployed to staging and smoke-tested against anonymized traces; behavior looks correct (header downmapped to metadata.priority=soft and no pool re-affinity). Pushing to prod tonight in a gated rollout for Integris account id.
- Marissa: I added an internal spec link (private) to the HubSpot deal (see related_links) with the proposed SDK flag semantics and API contract changes.
- Neha: Recommend the canary for Integris: disable client header on 5% of traffic and enable server-side downmap for the other 95% for 48 hours; then narrow to 100% server downmap if stable. Sam — do you agree to the canary cadence?

Sam Ortega (external) replied inline: "Yes — we can do the 5/95 canary tomorrow morning (06/13) and will monitor clinical flows. Thanks for the rapid response."

I'll keep the thread updated after the prod rollout.

—Soojin
Soojin Lee
Product Manager, Runtime Policies | Redwood Inference
